risk_if_not_implemented: Without Identification Requirement, unauthorized individuals may gain physical access to facilities and equipment, enabling theft, tampering, damage or safety incidents. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), System / Data Compromise (Non-Technical Vector) (R-BC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to natural threats NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-8, NT-11, NT-12, NT-13, NT-14; Physical Crime (MT-5), Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: Monitoring Physical Access
compensating_control_1.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor for, detect and respond to physical security incidents.
compensating_control_1.justification: Monitoring Physical Access (PES-13) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Identification Requirement (PES-14.2) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Visitor Control
compensating_control_2.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to identify, authorize and monitor visitors before allowing access to the facility (other than areas designated as publicly accessible).
compensating_control_2.justification: Visitor Control (PES-14) provides physical access control that compensates for the absence of Identification Requirement (PES-14.2) by preventing unauthorized physical interaction with systems and infrastructure. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
